evidence.observation: Kara Swisher denial: quote attributed to her in the book was confirmed by her as fabricated and never said.
evidence.provenance: Named subject direct denial to NYT
evidence.notes: Subject is a major media figure with direct standing to deny. Quote was a fabrication, not a misattribution.

evidence.observation: Paul Barrett denial: NYU Stern researcher confirmed quote attributed to him was not his.
Meredith Broussard quote was attributed to Wired but actually appeared in Columbia Journalism Review — wrong-outlet misattribution.
evidence.notes: Outlet-swapping is a signature LLM source-mixing failure pattern. Directly diagnostic for H6.

evidence.observation: Lee McIntyre quote was hybrid — partially real (existed elsewhere) plus altered wording inserted by author/tool. Mixed-mode failure.
Author Steven Rosenbaum pre-disclosed AI use as research assistance throughout the writing process — appears in book itself.
evidence.provenance: Author's own statement in published work
evidence.notes: Strongly weighs against deliberate manufactured-controversy framing — author would not pre-disclose if planning to hide AI use.

evidence.observation: Coverage framing across NYT/Futurism/Daily Beast emphasizes 'proves the thesis' irony — book about AI truth decay contains AI-fabricated quotes.
evidence.notes: Only piece of evidence with meaningful weight for H2 — and only on framing, not substance.

evidence.observation: Credentialing apparatus: Maria Ressa foreword (Nobel Peace Prize laureate), Atlantic CEO blurb, other establishment endorsements treated as substitute for fact-checking.
evidence.provenance: Visible on book jacket and front matter

evidence.observation: Rosenbaum is media establishment insider — past executive roles at Magnify Networks, Curate.us, AOL — credential standing reinforces credentialing shortcut at publishing pipeline level.

Prior pattern: Vandermeersch case — Dutch journalist fabricated quotes using ChatGPT in editorials over years, exposed March 2026. Establishes pattern of AI-quote-fabrication in published non-fiction.
evidence.notes: Prior-pattern evidence is the strongest support for H5 (genre artifact) framing.

evidence.observation: Errors trivially falsifiable by anyone who knows the named subjects — Swisher, Barrett, Broussard. Any competent fact-checker with a Rolodex catches these in one round of verification.
evidence.notes: Falsifiability of errors weighs strongly against H2 — a deliberate operation would use harder-to-catch errors.

evidence.observation: Errors cluster around high-citation-density sections (chapters quoting many figures) rather than being randomly distributed — proportional to volume of AI-assisted quote retrieval.
Same fabricated quotes propagated through aggregators and review sites before NYT investigation — circular amplification with no independent verification.
No external beneficiary identifiable — book sales would benefit from accuracy; author and publisher both take reputational damage from exposure; endorsers' reputations also damaged.
evidence.notes: Absence of beneficiary is the strongest single counter to H2.
